questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Italian culture and climate as well as Bologna's good reputation as a student city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: All the information you need is on their website. Basically, you only need to know where to find the courses in order to get your Learning Agreement signed. You will get all additional information after you perform the online check-in upon arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: You book an online check-in session, where you can ask questions. Further, you get a document describing all the things you need to do to sign up for the courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy enough if you are willing to pay for the student accomodations located right outside the city center. However, if you have the patience and time, it will be worth it to search for accomodation within the city walls.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You cannot live on campus in Bologna as campus is in the city center.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing situation is really bad in Bologna so make sure to start looking well in advance.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When you arrive, you book an appointment to check-in. Afterwards everything is straightforward.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: If you are impatient, you can contact the international office at UniBo through Teams on your UniBo account.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It is much more flexible than in Copenhagen. I changed my courses multiple times and it is easy.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not stress about anything. In theory you can sign up for courses until a few works before the exam.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: You can find really difficult courses matching the level of Economics in Copenhagen, but you can also choose not to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Not really any courses with regular exercise classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) Financial Products and Markets
2) Central Banking and Monetary Policy
3) Economics of Entrepreneurship
4) Law and Practice of Financial Transactions
5) Managerial Decision Through Machine Learning: A Primer in Python

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Python course was really good in my opinion. You learn basic Python and get to work with real data from Italian companies in the exam, which is a take home group exam.

questions.answer: La Dolce Vita

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not really look into what was offered by the University. But I know some people did their language courses and were content with those.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: ESN arranges a lot of activities for Erasmus students in Bologna.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to some of the ESN events. Talk to the Italians in your courses, they are usually very open and this way you get to know some Italians.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hike in the hills south of Bologna. Travel around by train to nearby cities; Parma, Verona, Florence, Venice etc. Rent a car and do a road trip in Tuscany. Go to Cinque Terre. Fly to Sicily.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk with them during breaks in the lectures.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The lively atmosphere in the city.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Do not stress too much about the planning before going.
2) Find accomodation in advance maybe reach out to ESN Bologna on instagram or WhatsApp to get help.
3) Explore Italy while in Bologna.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not order cappuccino after breakfast.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: International friends and learning to speak Italian.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Planning weekend trips in June, because you get the exam dates so late compared to in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy your stay.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
